<a id="ocean"></a>
## `ocean`

调用方式: `ocean --help`

```text
Usage: ocean [--profile] <name> [options] [app-args...]
       ocean plugin --profile <name> <pnpm-args...>

ocean: boot an Ocean profile — an ordered stack of plugin-bundle patch layers
under your own overrides.

Arguments:
  args                           arguments for the booted profile's app (see:
                                 ocean --profile <name> --help)

Options:
  -V, --version                  output the version number
  --profile <name>               the profile under $OCEAN_HOME/profiles to boot
  --from-default-profile <name>  replace a custom profile with a fresh copy of a
                                 shipped profile template
  --patch <path>                 extra patch-list overlay applied after the
                                 profile layer (repeatable)
  --dump-config                  print the composed profile tree and exit
  --dump-config-schema           print JSON Schema for profile entries and
                                 patches without mounting
  --dump-default-config          print the profile tree without its user layer
                                 or --patch overlays and exit

Examples:
  ocean web                                   boot the web profile (same as: ocean --profile web)
  ocean rescue --from-default-profile web
                                            recreate rescue from the shipped web template, then boot it
  ocean headless "run the tests"              answer one task, print the result, and exit
  ocean tui --patch ./extra.yml               boot a custom profile with one extra overlay
  ocean tui --resume <session>                arguments after the launcher flags reach the app
  ocean web --help                            the web app's own flags and help
  ocean plugin --profile tui add <package>    install a plugin into the tui profile

```

<a id="ocean-plugin"></a>
## `ocean plugin`

调用方式: `ocean plugin --help`

```text
Usage: ocean plugin [options] [args...]

manage a profile's plugins by forwarding the remaining arguments to pnpm in the
profile directory

Arguments:
  args              pnpm arguments, forwarded verbatim (add <pkg>, remove <pkg>,
                    why <pkg>, ...)

Options:
  --profile <name>  the profile whose plugins to manage (initialized on first
                    use)
  -h, --help        show this help
```

<a id="ocean-connect"></a>
## `ocean connect`

调用方式: `ocean connect --help`, `ocean connect help --help`, `ocean --profile connect --help`, `ocean --profile connect help --help`

```text
Usage: ocean connect [options] [command]

Run a command against an authenticated remote Ocean Host.

Options:
  --url <https-url>                                                           Ocean server address
  --token-env <name>                                                          environment variable containing the device token
  --token-stdin                                                               read the device token from redirected standard input
  --pair <link>                                                               pairing link from ocean remote-device pair; exchanges its one-time grant for a device token
  -h, --help                                                                  display help for command

Commands:
  list                                                                        List remote sessions as JSON
  create [options]                                                            Create a remote session
  history [options] <session-id>                                              Read a remote history page
  follow <session-id>                                                         Stream snapshots and live remote session history
  state <session-id>                                                          Read remote session and pending input state
  wait <session-id>                                                           Wait briefly for idle state or pending input
  files <session-id> [path]                                                   List files in a remote session workspace
  read [options] <session-id> <path>                                          Read a page of a text file on the Host
  upload <session-id> <local-path>                                            Stream a local file to the Host and return its prompt attachment receipt
  terminals <session-id>                                                      List terminals retained on the Host
  terminal-create [options] <session-id>                                      Create a terminal on the Host
  terminal-watch <session-id> <terminal-id>                                   Stream the current terminal screen and subsequent output as JSON lines
  terminal-write <session-id> <terminal-id> <text>                            Send one text input to a Host terminal and wait for acceptance
  terminal-close <session-id> <terminal-id>                                   Close a terminal on the Host
  approvals <session-id>                                                      List pending approvals for a remote session
  questions [options] <session-id>                                            List pending questions for a remote session
  answer-question [options] <session-id> <question-request-id> <answer-json>  Submit a structured answer to a pending remote question request
  approve <session-id> <approval-id> <allow-or-deny>                          Answer one approval in the specified remote session
  cancel <session-id>                                                         Cancel active work in the remote session
  prompt [options] <session-id> <text>                                        Submit or steer a prompt in a remote session
  help [command]                                                              display help for command
```

<a id="ocean-headless"></a>
## `ocean headless`

调用方式: `ocean headless --help`, `ocean --profile headless --help`

```text
Usage: ocean --profile headless [options] [task...]

Answer one task and exit; the answer goes to stdout and diagnostics to stderr.

Arguments:
  task                        the task text; multiple words are joined by
                              spaces, and `-` reads stdin

Options:
  --json                      write newline-delimited run events to stdout
                              instead of the final message
  --session-id <id>           adopt the persisted Session with this id; an
                              unknown id is an error
  --permission-mode <preset>  select a configured permission preset for this
                              task, including on resume
  --approval-policy <policy>  set approval behavior after selecting the
                              permission preset (choices: "ask", "never")
  --add-dir <path>            allow an additional physical absolute directory
                              under workspace-write (repeatable)
  -h, --help                  show this help

Examples:
  ocean --profile headless "run the tests"          answer one task and exit
  echo "run the tests" | ocean --profile headless   read the task from stdin
  ocean --profile headless --json "run the tests"   emit machine-readable run events
  ocean --profile headless --session-id session-… "continue"   resume an existing Session
  ocean --profile headless --permission-mode workspace-write --add-dir /repo/.git "commit the fix"
                                                        grant shared Git metadata for this task

```

<a id="ocean-remote-device"></a>
## `ocean remote-device`

调用方式: `ocean remote-device --help`, `ocean remote-device help --help`, `ocean --profile remote-device --help`, `ocean --profile remote-device help --help`

```text
Usage: ocean remote-device [options] [command]

Manage device access through a Host’s local socket, or bootstrap its local
credential store.

Options:
  --socket <path>           absolute path to the running Host administrator
                            socket
  --bootstrap               create or list devices using the local credential
                            store; supports Windows
  --timeout <milliseconds>  maximum time to wait for a socket operation and live
                            connection cleanup (default: 30000)
  -h, --help                display help for command

Commands:
  list                      List devices and their access state
  create [options] <label>  Create a device and return its token once
  pair [options] <label>    Create a one-time link that adds a device without
                            typing its token
  rotate <id>               Replace a device token and invalidate its existing
                            logins
  revoke <id>               Revoke a device and close its live connections
  help [command]            display help for command
```

<a id="ocean-remote-device-pair"></a>
## `ocean remote-device pair`

调用方式: `ocean remote-device pair --help`, `ocean --profile remote-device pair --help`

```text
Usage: ocean remote-device pair [options] <label>

Create a one-time link that adds a device without typing its token

Options:
  --url <https-url>  HTTPS address clients use to reach this Host, including any
                     mount path; the Host supplies its public URL when it has
                     one
  --scope <name>     a right the device holds; repeat to name several
                     (sessions:read, sessions:write, files:read, files:write,
                     terminal:operate, settings:manage); every right when absent
                     (default: [])
  --ttl <seconds>    how long the link stays valid, 30 to 3600; the Host default
                     applies otherwise
  --qr               also print a QR code of the browser link to standard error
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

<a id="ocean-serve"></a>
## `ocean serve`

调用方式: `ocean serve --help`, `ocean --profile serve --help`

```text
Usage: ocean serve [options]

Serve an Ocean Host with device authentication.

Options:
  --host <host>                  bind address: one concrete IPv4 or IPv6 literal
                                 of a local interface; wildcard addresses are
                                 rejected
  --port <port>                  listen port; pass 0 to let the OS pick a free
                                 one
  --public-url <url>             advertise this HTTP(S) root in the printed,
                                 opened, runtime-context, and OCEAN_WEB_URL
                                 forms; grants no trust
  --trusted-host <authority...>  extra authority the /api browser-trust fence
                                 accepts (host or host:port; repeatable)
  --tls-cert <file>              PEM server certificate chain; requires
                                 --tls-key
  --tls-key <file>               unencrypted PEM private key; requires
                                 --tls-cert
  --device-admin-socket <path>   owner-only local administrator socket
  --tailscale-serve              publish the loopback listener on this node's
                                 tailnet name over HTTPS through `tailscale
                                 serve`; replaces --public-url and TLS
  --tailscale-serve-port <port>  Tailscale HTTPS port for --tailscale-serve;
                                 default 443
  --tailscale-command <path>     Tailscale executable for --tailscale-serve,
                                 such as a wrapper that runs it with sudo;
                                 default tailscale
  -h, --help                     show this help

Examples:
  ocean serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3080
                                             serve on loopback without opening a browser
  ocean serve --host 10.0.0.7 --tls-cert ./server-chain.pem --tls-key ./server-key.pem
                                             serve HTTPS on one local interface
  ocean serve --tailscale-serve --device-admin-socket /absolute/path/admin.sock
                                             serve on loopback and publish https://<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net/
  ocean remote-device --socket /absolute/path/admin.sock create laptop
                                             create a device token through the local administrator socket
  ocean remote-device --socket /absolute/path/admin.sock pair laptop
                                             create a one-time link that adds a device

Non-loopback listeners require --tls-cert and --tls-key, or --tailscale-serve on loopback.
Use the local administrator socket to create device tokens; the server URL contains no
launch token.

```

<a id="ocean-web"></a>
## `ocean web`

调用方式: `ocean web --help`, `ocean --profile web --help`

```text
Usage: ocean --profile web [options]

Serve the Ocean browser UI.

Options:
  --host <host>                  bind address: one concrete IPv4 or IPv6 literal
                                 of a local interface; wildcard addresses are
                                 rejected
  --port <port>                  listen port; pass 0 to let the OS pick a free
                                 one
  --public-url <url>             advertise this HTTP(S) root in the printed,
                                 opened, runtime-context, and OCEAN_WEB_URL
                                 forms; grants no trust
  --trusted-host <authority...>  extra authority the /api browser-trust fence
                                 accepts (host or host:port; repeatable)
  --tls-cert <file>              PEM server certificate chain; requires
                                 --tls-key
  --tls-key <file>               unencrypted PEM private key; requires
                                 --tls-cert
  --no-open                      do not open the Web UI in the default browser
  -h, --help                     show this help

Examples:
  ocean --profile web                          serve on the composed host and port
  ocean --profile web --no-open                serve without opening a browser
  ocean --profile web --port 8080              serve on another port
  ocean --profile web --host 10.0.0.7          bind one local interface address
  ocean --profile web --public-url https://app.example/ui/ --trusted-host app.example
                                             advertise a prefix-stripping HTTPS proxy entry and admit its authority
  ocean --profile web --tls-cert ./server-chain.pem --tls-key ./server-key.pem
                                             serve HTTPS with an existing certificate and key

```
